headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and use MCP/network, while mem0 has no documented isolation or output filtering.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can ingest files and MCP/tool outputs, and mem0 is a knowledge-memory system with no documented isolation or provenance controls. If mem0 stores attacker-controlled text that Semantic Kernel later reads from a shared workspace or memory store, instructions can cross the boundary. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF mem0 content is written into a shared file or memory store that Semantic Kernel reads
IF Semantic Kernel treats retrieved text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all mem0-retrieved text before SK consumes it
Disable automatic tool execution on retrieved memory content
Separate mem0 storage from SK-readable workspaces
Require a human review step for any memory-derived instruction
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the integration layer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel has broad network egress and can read filesystem content, while mem0 is a memory system that may hold application context. If both share a workspace or memory store, sensitive context can flow from mem0 into SK and then out through SK's API calls. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets by default, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF mem0 stores sensitive application context in a location Semantic Kernel can read
IF Semantic Kernel forwards that context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Restrict SK to a redacted subset of mem0 data
Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Turn off outbound plugins for sensitive runs
Review outbound prompts for sensitive fields before execution
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0 itself shows no write or network surface, but Semantic Kernel can write files and use application-defined files plus MCP. If both agents target the same mutable workspace or memory-backed state, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt shared artifacts. The profiles do not show git writes, so high is not warranted, but overlapping mutable file access is enough for medium.
conditions: IF mem0 and Semantic Kernel write to the same directory or memory-backed artifact
IF multiple Semantic Kernel instances share the same memory store without locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Enable per-resource locking in the orchestrator
Serialize writes to shared memory
Use append-only logs instead of in-place edits
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is designed for agent/tool orchestration, so it may treat mem0-retrieved content as authoritative unless the integration adds verification. Mem0 can supply long-term memory, but the profiles do not show built-in validation or citation checking. That makes a default cascade plausible, though not clearly high because no downstream irreversible action is documented.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses mem0 output as a source of facts or instructions
IF no verification step is inserted before tool calls or user-facing actions
mitigations: Require citations for memory-derived claims
Insert a verification prompt before actions
Limit mem0 to retrieval-only mode
Log source IDs alongside every retrieved fact
requires-engineering: add a fact-checking gate before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials and can send data to third-party APIs, while mem0 is a memory store with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. If regulated data is stored in mem0 and then routed through SK plugins, retention or residency mismatches can occur. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 and later sent through Semantic Kernel plugins
IF the deployment requires residency, retention, or deletion guarantees not enforced by the integration
mitigations: Classify data before it enters mem0
Block regulated fields from outbound plugins
Document retention and deletion behavior for both systems
Use region-pinned endpoints where available
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention
